**Section 4: Reconciliation of Weighted Average to Certified Figure**

The difference between the weighted average net circulation (12,650 copies) and the ABC-certified figure (12,500 copies) is 150 copies. This difference arises from the treatment of the 27 December 2025 issue, which was published on a Saturday between the Christmas and New Year bank holidays. For this issue, 150 copies were distributed to the Christmas markets in Merebrook High Street and the surrounding villages as part of a promotional arrangement with the town council. The ABC rules do not permit these copies to be counted as paid circulation because they were given away free of charge to visitors. The circulation manager decided not to challenge this ruling, as the promotional value of the market distribution was considered to outweigh the small reduction in the certified figure. The 150 copies are therefore included in the free distribution column for December 2025 but excluded from the net circulation total.

**Section 5: Publication Schedule**

The editorial calendar for the Merebrook & District Recorder shows publication_days as Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Record status: current. This schedule is current and has been in operation since 1 April 2024. Prior to that date, the paper published on Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. The change was made to give readers a Saturday edition, which has proved popular with the farming community and with families attending weekend events.

The publication schedule is as follows:

- **Tuesday edition** — published every Tuesday, with the exception of the Tuesday following a bank holiday Monday, when publication is moved to Wednesday.
- **Thursday edition** — published every Thursday, with no exceptions other than force majeure events such as severe weather or industrial action at the print works.
- **Saturday edition** — published every Saturday, including bank holiday weekends, unless the print works is closed for a public holiday. In such cases, the Saturday edition is published on the Friday.

The editorial calendar is maintained by the newsroom coordinator and is reviewed quarterly. Any proposed change to the publication days must be approved by the publisher and notified to the distribution manager at least four weeks in advance. The current calendar is in force until 31 March 2027.

**Section 6: Deadlines**

Deadlines for each edition are set to allow the paper to be printed, bound, and dispatched to the distribution depot in time for the morning delivery rounds. The deadlines are as follows:

- **Tuesday edition** — editorial copy deadline Monday 15:00; advertising copy deadline Monday 17:00; final page proofs to the print works Monday 19:30; print run commences Monday 22:00; papers delivered to the depot Tuesday 03:30.
- **Thursday edition** — editorial copy deadline Wednesday 15:00; advertising copy deadline Wednesday 17:00; final page proofs to the print works Wednesday 19:30; print run commences Wednesday 22:00; papers delivered to the depot Thursday 03:30.
- **Saturday edition** — editorial copy deadline Friday 14:00; advertising copy deadline Friday 16:00; final page proofs to the print works Friday 18:30; print run commences Friday 21:00; papers delivered to the depot Saturday 03:00.

The earlier deadlines for the Saturday edition reflect the need to accommodate the larger classified advertising section, which is traditionally the biggest of the week. The newsroom coordinator is responsible for communicating any deadline changes to the editorial and advertising teams.

**Section 7: Distribution Planning**

Distribution planning is carried out by the distribution manager in conjunction with the circulation manager. The planning process covers the following areas:
**Merebrook & District Recorder – Circulation and Publication Records**

**Section 7: Distribution Planning (continued)**

The distribution manager prepares a provisional route plan for each edition no later than two working days before the print run commences. The plan is issued to the depot supervisor and to the heads of the three delivery teams. The plan lists, for each route, the number of bundles, the drop points, and the expected delivery completion time. Route plans are held on file for a minimum of twelve months for audit purposes.

The circulation manager is responsible for reconciling the number of copies printed against the number of copies distributed and the number of returns. The reconciliation is completed within three working days of the edition date. Any discrepancy greater than one half of one per cent of the print run is reported in writing to the publisher.

**Section 8: Returns and Unsold Copies**

Returns are collected by delivery teams at the end of each round and are brought to the depot. Returns are counted and recorded on the returns sheet, which is signed by the depot supervisor and countersigned by the circulation manager. Unsold copies are retained at the depot for seven days, after which they are pulped. The pulp contractor collects unsold copies on the first Tuesday of each month.

For the period January to June 2026, the average weekly return rate was 4.2 per cent of the print run. The highest single-edition return rate in this period was 6.8 per cent, recorded for the Saturday edition of 14 March 2026, when heavy rain disrupted the morning rounds. The lowest return rate was 2.9 per cent, recorded for the Thursday edition of 7 May 2026.

Return rates are reviewed monthly by the circulation manager. A sustained return rate above 5 per cent for any single edition triggers a review of the print run for that edition. No edition has been subject to such a review since the Saturday edition of 21 November 2025, for which the print run was reduced by 250 copies for the following four weeks.

**Section 9: Circulation Adjustments**

Circulation adjustments are made in response to changes in demand, returns, and distribution arrangements. Each adjustment is recorded in the circulation ledger with the edition date, the route or area affected, the number of copies added or removed, and the reason for the adjustment. The ledger is maintained by the circulation manager and is audited annually.

Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C). The press hall temperature is monitored
continuously by the building management system (BMS) and is also checked manually by
maintenance staff at the start of each shift.

The acceptable operating band for press hall temperature is 18.0°C to 24.0°C. The target
set-point is 21.0°C. Short-term excursions outside this band are permitted only where the
duration is less than 30 minutes and where the cause is being actively investigated.

The maintenance manual environmental log records Haslingdon Print Works
press_hall_temperature as 21.5 celsius. This value is the current controlled entry for the
press hall and is within the acceptable operating band. It is used as the reference point
for all temperature-related adjustments on the presses and ancillary equipment.

2.2.2 Relative Humidity

Relative humidity (RH) is measured as a percentage (%). The acceptable operating band is
45% to 65% RH. The target set-point is 55% RH.

Humidity is controlled by the steam injection system (SIS) located in the air handling
unit (AHU-2). The SIS is to be checked weekly for steam trap operation and for signs of
scale build-up in the injection nozzles.

2.2.3 Air Pressure Differential

The press hall is maintained at a slight positive pressure relative to the reel store and
the outside, to prevent the ingress of dust and paper fibres. The target differential is
+15 Pa (Pascals) relative to the reel store and +20 Pa relative to outside.

Differential pressure is monitored by a manometer mounted on the wall adjacent to the
main entrance door (location code M-02). Readings are to be recorded on the daily
environmental checklist.

2.2.4 Air Changes per Hour

The ventilation system is designed to provide a minimum of 6 air changes per hour in the
occupied area of the press hall. This is verified annually by the ventilation testing
contractor and the report is retained in the maintenance office.

The maintenance manual environmental log records Haslingdon Print Works press_hall_temperature as 21.5 celsius. Record status: current.

2.3 Monitoring Equipment

2.3.1 Building Management System (BMS)

The BMS is the primary monitoring system for press hall environmental conditions.
Sensors are located as follows:

- BMS-T-01: Temperature sensor, mounted on the north wall, 3.5 m above floor level, near

- BMS-T-02: Temperature sensor, mounted on the south wall, 3.5 m above floor level, near

- BMS-H-01: Humidity sensor, mounted adjacent to BMS-T-01.
- BMS-H-02: Humidity sensor, mounted adjacent to BMS-T-02.
- BMS-DP-01: Differential pressure sensor, located in the air handling unit return
  duct.

The BMS records data at 15-minute intervals. Data is stored on the BMS server and is
retained for a minimum of 12 months. Access to historical data is available to
maintenance engineers and the shift manager through the BMS workstation in the control
room.

A portable temperature and humidity meter (instrument code PT-3) is kept in the

3.3 Lubrication Schedule

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's lubrication
chart (drawing no. KBA-CM-62-LUB, revision 4) and the schedule below. Only
lubricants listed in the approved lubricants list (Appendix B of this manual) shall
be used. Substitutes are not permitted without the written approval of the
maintenance manager.

The central lubrication system (automatic) serves the main bearings, impression
cylinders, and folder rollers. The system reservoir is to be checked at the start of
each shift and topped up as necessary. The system shall be set to deliver the
manufacturer's specified quantity of oil per cycle; the delivery rate is checked
during the weekly service.

3.3.1 Daily Lubrication (Operator Checks)

a) Check the oil level in the central lubrication system reservoir. Top up with
   ISO VG 220 oil if the level is below the "MIN" mark on the sight glass.

b) Grease the reel stand spindle bearings (two nipples per stand) with lithium
   grease, two strokes of the grease gun.

c) Check the oil level in the folder gearbox sight glass. Top up with ISO VG 150
   oil if necessary.

3.3.2 Weekly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the delivery chain guides (six nipples per press) with lithium grease.

b) Grease the folder former board adjustment screws (four nipples per folder) with
   lithium grease.

c) Check the central lubrication system delivery rate. The system shall deliver
   not less than 0.5 litres per hour at normal running speed. Record the measured
   rate on Form M-3.

d) Grease the reel stand lifting arm pivots (two nipples per stand).

3.3.3 Monthly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the angle bar rollers (twelve nipples per press) with lithium grease.

b) Grease the compensator roller bearings (four nipples per press).

c) Check the oil level in the dampening solution circulation pump gearboxes
   (one per unit). Top up with ISO VG 68 oil if necessary.

The manufacturer's specification for the Koenig & Bauer Commander 6/2 states a maintenance_interval of 500000 impressions. Record status: current.

d) Grease the folder jaw cam followers (six nipples per folder).

3.3.4 Quarterly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the main drive motor bearings (two nipples per motor) with lithium
   grease.

b) Grease the blanket cylinder bearing housings (four nipples per unit) with
   lithium grease, taking care not to over-grease.

c) Check the oil in the folder stitcher gearbox. Top up with ISO VG 150 oil if
   necessary.

d) Grease the reel stand pivot bearings (two nipples per stand).

3.4 Major Service – 500,000 Impressions

The major service is to be carried out when the impression counter reaches the
interval specified in Section 3.2. The service shall be planned so that it does not
interrupt production unless unavoidable. The maintenance manager shall agree a
service window with the production manager at least two weeks in advance.

The major service comprises the following operations:

a) Replace the blanket cylinder packings and check the cylinder alignment.

b) Replace the impression cylinder gripper pads and check the gripper timing.

c) Replace the folder jaw blades and check the jaw timing.

d) Replace the delivery chain and sprockets.

e) Replace the dampening roller covers.

f) Check the reel stand braking system and replace the brake pads if worn.

g) Check the tension of all drive belts and replace as necessary.

**Section 4: Reconciliation of Weighted Average to Certified Figure**

The difference between the weighted average net circulation (12,650 copies) and the ABC-certified figure (12,500 copies) is 150 copies. This difference arises from the treatment of the 27 December 2025 issue, which was published on a Saturday between the Christmas and New Year bank holidays. For this issue, 150 copies were distributed to the Christmas markets in Merebrook High Street and the surrounding villages as part of a promotional arrangement with the town council. The ABC rules do not permit these copies to be counted as paid circulation because they were given away free of charge to visitors. The circulation manager decided not to challenge this ruling, as the promotional value of the market distribution was considered to outweigh the small reduction in the certified figure. The 150 copies are therefore included in the free distribution column for December 2025 but excluded from the net circulation total.

**Section 5: Publication Schedule**

The editorial calendar for the Merebrook & District Recorder shows publication_days as Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Record status: current. This schedule is current and has been in operation since 1 April 2024. Prior to that date, the paper published on Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. The change was made to give readers a Saturday edition, which has proved popular with the farming community and with families attending weekend events.

The publication schedule is as follows:

- **Tuesday edition** — published every Tuesday, with the exception of the Tuesday following a bank holiday Monday, when publication is moved to Wednesday.
- **Thursday edition** — published every Thursday, with no exceptions other than force majeure events such as severe weather or industrial action at the print works.
- **Saturday edition** — published every Saturday, including bank holiday weekends, unless the print works is closed for a public holiday. In such cases, the Saturday edition is published on the Friday.

The editorial calendar is maintained by the newsroom coordinator and is reviewed quarterly. Any proposed change to the publication days must be approved by the publisher and notified to the distribution manager at least four weeks in advance. The current calendar is in force until 31 March 2027.

**Section 6: Deadlines**

Deadlines for each edition are set to allow the paper to be printed, bound, and dispatched to the distribution depot in time for the morning delivery rounds. The deadlines are as follows:

- **Tuesday edition** — editorial copy deadline Monday 15:00; advertising copy deadline Monday 17:00; final page proofs to the print works Monday 19:30; print run commences Monday 22:00; papers delivered to the depot Tuesday 03:30.
- **Thursday edition** — editorial copy deadline Wednesday 15:00; advertising copy deadline Wednesday 17:00; final page proofs to the print works Wednesday 19:30; print run commences Wednesday 22:00; papers delivered to the depot Thursday 03:30.
- **Saturday edition** — editorial copy deadline Friday 14:00; advertising copy deadline Friday 16:00; final page proofs to the print works Friday 18:30; print run commences Friday 21:00; papers delivered to the depot Saturday 03:00.

The earlier deadlines for the Saturday edition reflect the need to accommodate the larger classified advertising section, which is traditionally the biggest of the week. The newsroom coordinator is responsible for communicating any deadline changes to the editorial and advertising teams.

**Section 7: Distribution Planning**

Distribution planning is carried out by the distribution manager in conjunction with the circulation manager. The planning process covers the following areas:

**Section 7: Distribution Planning (continued)**

The distribution manager prepares a provisional route plan for each edition no later than two working days before the print run commences. The plan is issued to the depot supervisor and to the heads of the three delivery teams. The plan lists, for each route, the number of bundles, the drop points, and the expected delivery completion time. Route plans are held on file for a minimum of twelve months for audit purposes.

The circulation manager is responsible for reconciling the number of copies printed against the number of copies distributed and the number of returns. The reconciliation is completed within three working days of the edition date. Any discrepancy greater than one half of one per cent of the print run is reported in writing to the publisher.

**Section 8: Returns and Unsold Copies**

Returns are collected by delivery teams at the end of each round and are brought to the depot. Returns are counted and recorded on the returns sheet, which is signed by the depot supervisor and countersigned by the circulation manager. Unsold copies are retained at the depot for seven days, after which they are pulped. The pulp contractor collects unsold copies on the first Tuesday of each month.

For the period January to June 2026, the average weekly return rate was 4.2 per cent of the print run. The highest single-edition return rate in this period was 6.8 per cent, recorded for the Saturday edition of 14 March 2026, when heavy rain disrupted the morning rounds. The lowest return rate was 2.9 per cent, recorded for the Thursday edition of 7 May 2026.

Return rates are reviewed monthly by the circulation manager. A sustained return rate above 5 per cent for any single edition triggers a review of the print run for that edition. documents.content:
Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C). The press hall temperature is monitored
continuously by the building management system (BMS) and is also checked manually by
maintenance staff at the start of each shift.

The acceptable operating band for press hall temperature is 18.0°C to 24.0°C. The target
set-point is 21.0°C. Short-term excursions outside this band are permitted only where the
duration is less than 30 minutes and where the cause is being actively investigated.

The maintenance manual environmental log records Haslingdon Print Works
press_hall_temperature as 21.5 celsius. This value is the current controlled entry for the
press hall and is within the acceptable operating band. It is used as the reference point
for all temperature-related adjustments on the presses and ancillary equipment.

2.2.2 Relative Humidity

Relative humidity (RH) is measured as a percentage (%). The acceptable operating band is
45% to 65% RH. The target set-point is 55% RH.

Humidity is controlled by the steam injection system (SIS) located in the air handling
unit (AHU-2). The SIS is to be checked weekly for steam trap operation and for signs of
scale build-up in the injection nozzles.

2.2.3 Air Pressure Differential

The press hall is maintained at a slight positive pressure relative to the reel store and
the outside, to prevent the ingress of dust and paper fibres. The target differential is
+15 Pa (Pascals) relative to the reel store and +20 Pa relative to outside.

Differential pressure is monitored by a manometer mounted on the wall adjacent to the
main entrance door (location code M-02). Readings are to be recorded on the daily
environmental checklist.

2.2.4 Air Changes per Hour

The ventilation system is designed to provide a minimum of 6 air changes per hour in the
occupied area of the press hall. This is verified annually by the ventilation testing
contractor and the report is retained in the maintenance office.

The maintenance manual environmental log records Haslingdon Print Works press_hall_temperature as 21.5 celsius. Record status: current.

2.3 Monitoring Equipment

2.3.1 Building Management System (BMS)

The BMS is the primary monitoring system for press hall environmental conditions.
Sensors are located as follows:

- BMS-T-01: Temperature sensor, mounted on the north wall, 3.5 m above floor level, near
  the KBA-2 delivery end.
- BMS-T-02: Temperature sensor, mounted on the south wall, 3.5 m above floor level, near
  the KBA-4 reel stand.
- BMS-H-01: Humidity sensor, mounted adjacent to BMS-T-01.
- BMS-H-02: Humidity sensor, mounted adjacent to BMS-T-02.
- BMS-DP-01: Differential pressure sensor, located in the air handling unit return
  duct.

The BMS records data at 15-minute intervals. Data is stored on the BMS server and is
retained for a minimum of 12 months. Access to historical data is available to
maintenance engineers and the shift manager through the BMS workstation in the control
room.

2.3.2 Portable Instruments

A portable temperature and humidity meter (instrument code PT-3) is kept in the
maintenance office. This is used for manual spot checks and for verifying the accuracy of
the BMS sensors. The PT-3 is to be calibrated annually and the calibration certificate is
filed in the instrument register.

2.3.3 Calibration Schedule

All environmental monitoring instruments are subject to the following calibration
schedule:

| BMS-T-02 | South wall | 12 months | April 2025 |

3.3 Lubrication Schedule

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's lubrication
chart (drawing no. KBA-CM-62-LUB, revision 4) and the schedule below. Only
lubricants listed in the approved lubricants list (Appendix B of this manual) shall
be used. Substitutes are not permitted without the written approval of the
maintenance manager.

The central lubrication system (automatic) serves the main bearings, impression
cylinders, and folder rollers. The system reservoir is to be checked at the start of
each shift and topped up as necessary. The system shall be set to deliver the
manufacturer's specified quantity of oil per cycle; the delivery rate is checked
during the weekly service.

3.3.1 Daily Lubrication (Operator Checks)

a) Check the oil level in the central lubrication system reservoir. Top up with
   ISO VG 220 oil if the level is below the "MIN" mark on the sight glass.

b) Grease the reel stand spindle bearings (two nipples per stand) with lithium
   grease, two strokes of the grease gun.

c) Check the oil level in the folder gearbox sight glass. Top up with ISO VG 150
   oil if necessary.

3.3.2 Weekly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the delivery chain guides (six nipples per press) with lithium grease.

b) Grease the folder former board adjustment screws (four nipples per folder) with
   lithium grease.

c) Check the central lubrication system delivery rate. The system shall deliver
   not less than 0.5 litres per hour at normal running speed. Record the measured
   rate on Form M-3.

d) Grease the reel stand lifting arm pivots (two nipples per stand).

3.3.3 Monthly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the angle bar rollers (twelve nipples per press) with lithium grease.

b) Grease the compensator roller bearings (four nipples per press).

c) Check the oil level in the dampening solution circulation pump gearboxes
   (one per unit). Top up with ISO VG 68 oil if necessary.

The manufacturer's specification for the Koenig & Bauer Commander 6/2 states a maintenance_interval of 500000 impressions. Record status: current.

d) Grease the folder jaw cam followers (six nipples per folder).

3.3.4 Quarterly Lubrication (Maintenance Fitter)

a) Grease the main drive motor bearings (two nipples per motor) with lithium
   grease.

b) Grease the blanket cylinder bearing housings (four nipples per unit) with
   lithium grease, taking care not to over-grease.

c) Check the oil in the folder stitcher gearbox. Top up with ISO VG 150 oil if
   necessary.

d) Grease the reel stand pivot bearings (two nipples per stand).

3.4 Major Service – 500,000 Impressions

The major service is to be carried out when the impression counter reaches the
interval specified in Section 3.2. The service shall be planned so that it does not
interrupt production unless unavoidable. The maintenance manager shall agree a
service window with the production manager at least two weeks in advance.

The major service comprises the following operations:

a) Replace the blanket cylinder packings and check the cylinder alignment.

b) Replace the impression cylinder gripper pads and check the gripper timing.

c) Replace the folder jaw blades and check the jaw timing.

d) Replace the delivery chain and sprockets.

e) Replace the dampening roller covers.

f) Check the reel stand braking system and replace the brake pads if worn.

g) Check the tension of all drive belts and replace as necessary.
